Honestly, this feels like pure speculation wrapped in hype at this point. We've already made our mark in 2024 and 2025, and I don't care if they ship $57B next quarter, provided the pricing power and margins don't turn into a massive cash burn cycle while they try to balance the books on paper. If they can actually justify the premium we are paying with real moats rather than just more AI compute cycles, that's the kind of story that defines a decade-long holding rather than a single day's trading session. Good call on the guidance, but don't sleep on the valuation gap if this doesn't drive new margins by next year.

When Nvidia finally builds the stuff to run the fullstack AI workloads, they'll own the market. We'll see how much growth actually materializes next quarter, because the only thing that matters in three years is whether the data centers stay plugged in. Long game, baby.

Honestly, $57B is just the appetizer, folks. The real value comes from how many more years Blackwell can run in silicon without hitting the end-of-life cliff.
